searchText: Different take, possibly because my infra is far smaller: Not at all. There are things that have to be in place for merge (mev boost, priority fee recipient), but they’re largely outside my control. The CL:EL update itself is going to be pretty easy, I expect. On the ice age: 12 months and push it back with every fork sounds eminently reasonable. For the next 5 years or so there’s so much big stuff that I expect forks more frequently anyway, and once things simmer down it’s good to have at least yearly releases. This time can always be adjusted. Do not like the idea of slot time increase. Gas limit would be interesting as it directly impacts validator earnings while not messing with consensus. I’d pretty strongly prefer a mechanism that doesn’t impact consensus at all, no “finality is gone you now need 100% participation” shenanigans. Gas limit can always be voted higher by validators as well if they want to side step the bomb. I think that’s okay. I really see it more as a mechanism to encourage at least yearly releases, than some sort of check against validator behavior IIRC your business is only about Eth2 staking, which makes you quite biased towards the fork schedule, as your sole focus is Ethereum. I was talking mostly as a busy medium-large business that doesn’t have time to play with testnets, participate in early testing (although that can be arguable), experimenting, etc. Yep absolutely. Much smaller scale. Oh, forgot to add important thing - businesses that focus on crypto in general, not just Ethereum. Scale doesn't really matter imo, although may be wrong here. Arguable whether we do. We are on multiple chains, EVM compatible and not. But it’s all either Oracle stuff or some staking stuff Playing with testnets is part of it, because there’s an Ethereum and Gnosis (might as well be Ethereum) staking setup. Which will change post merge … good to know what we’re walking into. On the Oracle side it’s not terribly involved. Solana either works or doesn’t; and then it needs a restart. Same for other chains. I have really come to appreciate the stability of Ethereum’s clients. We’re a reasonably busy tiny-smol business. Currently two technical people, soonish hopefully four. Plus one more business oriented founder. 9 chains for Oracle, plus another 4?5? for Proof of Reserves, and just two chains for staking. Right now there’s every reason to think about merge and get ready for it. At a different scale or broader setup overall that might change. Solana isn't a great example 😅 It brings a trollish chuckle every time it gets taken down by an NFT bot or something similarly silly Aaaanyway. I feel like waving my business model around doesn’t belong in this channel. Shall stop. I really love Geth, but to be honest stability is not so great in my experience. But it is definitely the best among rapidly-changing blockchains what Ethereum is among of. Interesting. Maybe for another channel to talk stability. It’s been rock solid for us, but we don’t do anything particularly crazy on the RPC side. For starters we don’t offer public RPC. We use a forked Geth, so it could be us who screwed things up and ruined the stability 😂 Although that's unlikely, since changes are minimal. I would really want to see more discussions about what power users (aka infra providers) want to have in Ethereum. (**not** regular users, otherwise we will have 1559-mining v2) Not in ACD though, but in this discord server in general. <#595721451651465227> perhaps Sorry, but to me <#595721451651465227> is a trashcan all devs are sending people to when someone starts talking on controversial topics. No channels on here are a trashcan. <#595721451651465227> is just for discussions that don't fit elsewhere. I.e. trashcan of this server 😅 I must say, this discussion about the purpose of <#595721451651465227>, can't you have that in <#595721451651465227> ? Hello, i am trying to make article about remaining issues which are keeping the merge from launch. Or issues which needs to solved? Any lead Thanks <@379253092719263744> i covered a bunch of them here: https://hackmd.io/@timbeiko/acd-update-011 if you want to be more granular, I recommend scanning the different channels under the `Merge` category, along with the various specs/testing repos Thank you, I had already read that. I will try Merge channel. Already moved there Bomb under PoS makes ethereum fragile. It made sense under PoW because miners are an external unaligned entity and it's only a temp phase. Eth stakers are directly invested in ethereum. The only after-merge feature that's directly necessary for ethereum to survive are withdrawals. Sounds grim, but right now if a bomb goes off at devcon or some other major ethereum conference ethereum is over. Same with circumstances that make it impossible to coordinate a fork (what if WW3 starts and every single core dev below 60 is drafted?). There would be nobody left with enough social capital to coordinate an obviously dominant fork. Without a bomb, ethereum would just survive as-is potentially forever. Alternatively, right now it's very hard to reject a fork with eg. forced kyc if all main devs were to be forced by their governments. It's much, much easier for normal users to reject a bad fork than it is to organize a competing one. I hope that war in Ukraine is enough empirical proof that history hasn't ended and extreme deviations from the status quo can indeed happen. For these reasons I think difficulty bomb should be gone forever when the merge happens. I’m pretty eth stakers will be as lazy uninformed and uninterested as miners it would be insane to expect different. Bomb that gets pushed back every fork and goes off after a year makes sense since that’s a 6 month safety margin. And worst case even if the devs are busy validators can get together to push it back. Particularly if it’s a gas bomb, “all it takes” is validators coordinating to raise the gas limit higher and higher to counteract the bomb. They won’t when everything is smooth, but have the option to when this feared wurst case scenario happens
